ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: the impulse response h(t) given in the figure is a piecewise rectangular waveform: in the interval from t=0 to t=1 the amplitude is +A, in the interval from t=1 to t=2 the amplitude is -A, in the interval from t=2 to t=3 the amplitude is +A, and at all other times it is 0. Then reason: the input is zero-mean white Gaussian noise, with two-sided power spectral density N0/2. After white noise passes through an LTI filter, the variance of the output noise at any time is Var[y(t)] = (N0/2) ∫ |h(λ)|^2 dλ. From the image, the energy of h(t) is A^2·1 + (-A)^2·1 + A^2·1 = 3A^2. Therefore the output noise variance at t=4 is (N0/2)·3A^2 = (3/2)A^2N0.

method.method_draft: First describe the plotted impulse response as three rectangular pulses: +A on [0,1], -A on [1,2], and +A on [2,3]. From the text, the input noise is zero-mean WGN with PSD N0/2 and the asked quantity is the filtered-noise variance at t=4. Apply the time-domain variance formula for an LTI-filtered white noise: Var[y(4)] = (N0/2)∫|h(λ)|^2 dλ. Compute the energy from the graph: A^2·1 + A^2·1 + A^2·1 = 3A^2. Multiply by N0/2 to obtain 3A^2N0/2.
